name: Yashoda
role: Foster-mother of Krishna in the Bhagavata Purana
summary: Yashoda, wife of the cowherd chief Nanda, is the loving foster-mother who raises the child Krishna in Gokul and Vrindavan. Many of the best-loved childhood stories of Krishna are set in her home.
about: In the Bhagavata Purana and the Harivamsa, Yashoda is the wife of Nanda, chief of the cowherds of Gokul. The texts tell that Vasudeva carried the newborn Krishna to her house on the night Kamsa's prison held him, and that she woke to find a baby at her side. She raises Krishna and Balarama as her own. Her house is the stage for the butter-stealing, the cosmos seen in Krishna's mouth and the tying to the grinding mortar. The Bhagavata Purana says her love is so complete that she never thinks of Krishna as God. Her name is explained as giver of fame. A regional tradition says she was reborn as Vakula Devi, mother of Venkateshvara, so that she could attend a wedding she had missed.
kidSummary: Yashoda is Krishna's foster-mother, a cowherd's wife who looked after him in the village of Gokul. In the stories she scolds him for stealing butter, laughs at his tricks and loves him more than anything. She is remembered as the picture of a caring mother.

story.title: A baby at her side
story.text: One night Yashoda falls asleep tired after the birth of her own daughter. When she wakes, a little boy named Krishna is lying beside her, and she welcomes him as her son.

story.title: The butter pot
story.text: While the helpers are busy, Yashoda churns the curd herself. Krishna gets cross when she leaves him to rescue boiling milk, so he breaks the pot and shares the butter with the monkeys.

story.title: The rope that is too short
story.text: Yashoda chases Krishna, catches him and decides to tie him to a big grinding mortar. Each rope she brings is just two fingers too short, until Krishna lets her tie him.

story.title: The whole world in a mouth
story.text: The boys complain that Krishna ate mud. Yashoda tells him to open his mouth and sees the whole universe inside. She is amazed, but soon forgets and hugs her little boy again.

story.title: A mother's love
story.text: The Bhagavata Purana says her simple love for Krishna won a kindness that even great gods did not get. That is why she is the favourite mother in many songs.

teaches: Patience when little ones are naughty
Simple love matters more than power
emblems: Rope and grinding mortar (the Damodara story)

facts.text: In the Bhagavata Purana the boys tell Yashoda that Krishna ate mud. She asks him to open his mouth and sees the whole universe inside, yet Yogamaya soon makes her forget it so she can cuddle her son again.
When she tried to tie Krishna to a mortar, the Bhagavata Purana says every rope was too short by exactly two finger-widths, however many she joined together.
The text says Krishna finally allowed himself to be tied when he saw how tired his mother was, sweating with flowers falling from her hair.
When milk boiled over, she left Krishna unfed to save it. The text says he then broke the curd pot with a stone and went off to eat butter in private.
When Yashoda found him, the Bhagavata Purana says he was on an upturned mortar handing out butter to monkeys, nervously watching for her.

Her tying of Krishna to the mortar led to the freeing of two cursed sons of Kubera, Nalakuvara and Manigriva: the dragged mortar jammed between a pair of arjuna trees, the trees fell and the two emerged.

In the Bhagavata Purana, baby Krishna was napping in a cradle under a cart while Yashoda was busy with a household ritual; his kicking legs sent the cart crashing and the neighbour children ran to tell her.
At the Kurukshetra eclipse gathering, the Bhagavata Purana says Krishna and Balarama hugged Yashoda but were too choked to speak, and Rohini and Devaki told her that her kindness could not be repaid.
The 1975 Telugu film Yashoda Krishna, directed by C. S. Rao, was about her bond with the child; the child Krishna was played by the actress Sridevi.
A regional tradition says she missed Krishna's wedding, so he promised she would see one. In Kali Yuga she is said to be reborn as Vakula Devi, who attends the wedding of Venkateshvara.
The Bhagavata Purana says Yashoda saw the universe in Krishna's mouth twice: first when baby Krishna yawned while nursing, then again after the mud complaint. The first time her heart pounded.

At one year old, Krishna suddenly felt as heavy as a mountain, so Yashoda set him down and prayed. A whirlwind demon, Trinavarta, swept him skyward but could not bear the weight, says the Bhagavata Purana.
Devotees explain the name Damodara, 367th in the Vishnu Sahasranama, as roped around the belly, after Yashoda tied him. Many sing the Damodarashtakam in the month of Kartika.
When Krishna's friend Uddhava visited Vraja, the Bhagavata Purana says Yashoda wept as she heard Nanda recall her son's deeds, and her love was so strong that milk flowed from her.
When Krishna lay in the coils of the serpent Kaliya, the Bhagavata Purana says the older women had to hold his mother back by force, so completely was her mind fixed on her son.
In Odisha and West Bengal the day after Janmashtami is called Nanda Ucchhaba, a joyful celebration of Krishna's foster parents Nanda and Yashoda. In north India the same day is Nandotsava.
A Tamil devotional song wonders what penance Yashoda performed to raise Krishna as her own. The Carnatic song Thaaye Yashoda gives voice to the neighbours' complaints about his mischief.
Puranic texts describe Yashoda as the sister of Rohini, Balarama's mother. In the Bhagavata Purana the two women look after both toddlers together in Nanda's home.

As crawling babies, Krishna and Balarama followed anyone wearing ankle bells, taking them for their mothers, then hurried back to Yashoda and Rohini when they saw a stranger, says the Bhagavata Purana.
Neighbouring women told Yashoda that Krishna let calves loose before milking, shared stolen curd with monkeys, and poked holes in pots he could not empty. The Bhagavata Purana lists these complaints.

quiz.q: What did Yashoda see when Krishna opened his mouth?
quiz.why: The Bhagavata Purana says she saw the entire cosmos, then forgot it.

quiz.q: What was wrong with the ropes Yashoda used to tie Krishna?
options: They were two finger-widths too short
quiz.why: However many she joined, each rope fell short by the same small amount.
Nanda was the cowherd chief of Gokul.

quiz.q: Which name of Krishna refers to the rope tied around his belly?
quiz.why: Vaishnava devotees link the name Damodara to Yashoda tying him with a rope.

quiz.q: What does the name Yashoda mean?
quiz.why: It comes from yash (fame) and da (giver).
